idiom_name: Dapper.Contrib extension methods (Insert/Update/Delete/Get) over a POCO
implementation_notes: The library supplies the record's missing CRUD: Dapper.Contrib adds Insert, Update, Delete, DeleteAll and Get/GetAll as IDbConnection extension methods, driven by [Key]/[ExplicitKey]/[Table]/[Column] attributes, so the POCO itself stays free of SQL while still owning its own persistence. What replaces the classic structure is a micro-ORM's extension methods instead of a base class - the object carries no session, so the connection (and any transaction) is passed in by the caller. Castle ActiveRecord historically provided the base-class form; the .NET mainstream choice, EF Core's DbContext with change tracking, is the data-mapper alternative and is the reason base-class Active Record is rare here.
pitfalls: A missing [Key] attribute makes Insert throw at runtime, and Update writes every mapped column, so a partially filled POCO overwrites columns with stale values.
Every call is its own round trip with no unit of work: wrap coupled writes in an IDbTransaction (or TransactionScope) yourself, since Dapper.Contrib commits per statement.
Because the entity is a plain POCO with no identity map, two instances of the same row race each other; a rowversion column plus a WHERE check is the usual guard.
